profile.summary: An endemic, much-branched shrub of open forest, scrub and rocky places. It can reach about three metres.
profile.lookFor: Alternate oval-to-rounded leaves have white woolly undersides; small creamy flower heads gather into rounded clusters.
profile.nameNote: Niniao is documented by DOC and Flora of New Zealand. Helichrysum glomeratum and Helichrysum aggregatum are historical names listed in the botanical references.

profile.summary: An endemic small tree found across New Zealand. Young plants form a dense mesh of zigzagging twigs before developing a more open adult crown.
profile.lookFor: Juvenile leaves are tiny with lobed tips; adult leaves are larger but retain small lobes or teeth near their ends.

profile.summary: An endemic tall tussock of the South Island, especially eastern and southern hill and mountain grasslands.
profile.lookFor: Long narrow golden-green leaves sweep outward from a dense base; tall flowering stems carry open branched panicles.
profile.nameNote: Wī kura is documented by Wikipedia and a Dunedin City Council planting schedule. WRT’s Hunangamoho was not confirmed for this species; NZPCN applies that shared name to Chionochloa conspicua. Flora recognises two subspecies; this profile does not assign WRT stock to either.
